newsitem.title: EGYPT: Italy's Prodi in Cairo for Mideast peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi in Cairo for Mideast peace talks.

text.p: Italy's Prime Minister Romano Prodi arrived in Cairo on Sunday for talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and Arab officials on the Middle East peace process, sources at Cairo airport said.
Prodi is expected to hold talks with Arab League Secretary-General Esmat Abdel Meguid on Sunday. He is also scheduled to meet Mubarak and Egyptian counterpart Kamal Ganzouri before leaving on Monday.
Prodi's visit to Egypt is his first to the Middle East, where Italy is eager to play a greater role in the peace process, since he was appointed prime minister in May.

It is also part of a flurry of diplomatic efforts by the European Union to boost its role in the peace talks, co-sponsored by the United States. Italy is the former head of the rotating EU presidency.
Arabs have traditionally seen the U.S. role in the Middle East as tilted towards Israel but the 15-nation bloc has said it would work, and not compete, with the American peace efforts.
Earlier this month, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat met Prodi to rally his support for the peace process.
Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini will also visit Israel on October 27 at the invitation of his counterpart David Levy.
